name: ICICI Bank Ltd
about: ICICI Bank is the second-largest private sector bank in India offering a diversified portfolio of financial products and services to retail, SME and corporate customers. The Bank has an extensive network of branches, ATMs and other touch-points.The ICICI group has presence in businesses like life and general insurance, housing finance, primary dealership, etc, through its subsidiaries and associates. [1]

sections.one_liner: India's #2 private bank. Profit growth is re-accelerating (+21% YoY), but loans now outrun deposits by 5.6pp.
business: Lends to and takes deposits from retail, business banking/SME, corporate and wealth clients; loans ₹15.54 lakh cr, deposits ₹17.95 lakh cr at Mar-26 [AR FY26]
Consolidated basis includes life and general insurance, housing finance and primary dealership subsidiaries; segment revenue shares not disclosed [AR FY26]
Earns net interest income (Q4 FY26 ₹22,979 cr, NIM 4.32%) plus fees (₹6,779 cr); 72-78% of fees from retail/rural/business banking [Q4FY26 call]
India-focused with overseas branches for India-linked business; 7,511 business centres after adding 528 in FY26 [AR FY26]
financial_snapshot: Sep-26 quarter: revenue ₹55,992 cr (+16.2% YoY, +7.2% QoQ), PAT ₹17,389 cr (+21.4% YoY), the fastest PAT growth in eight quarters [Numbers]
TTM: revenue ₹2,06,191 cr, PAT ₹62,827 cr; H1 FY27 PAT ₹33,665 cr, +17.0% YoY [Numbers]
OPM/EBITDA are negative (-12% to -29%) because of how bank financials are mapped; not meaningful. Use ROE 15.9% and NIM 4.36% instead [Numbers]
Mcap ₹10.0 lakh cr; stated P/E 16.9x, but TTM P/E computes to 15.9x; P/B 2.6x (₹1,394/₹540); dividend yield 0.87% [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR is 17.3% (3y) and 17.0% (5y); PAT CAGR is 17.8% and 23.3%, so PAT growth exceeded revenue growth over 5 years [Numbers]
FY26 slowed sharply: revenue +4.8%, PAT +6.2%; quarterly revenue YoY fell from 15.1% (Dec-24) to 2.5% (Mar-26) [Numbers]
Recovery is clear: revenue YoY went 2.5% → 6.4% → 16.2% and PAT YoY went 9.2% → 12.6% → 21.4% over the last three quarters [Numbers]
Loan growth went 11.5% (Q3 FY26) → 15.8% (Q4) → 19.6% (Q1 FY27); business banking grew 28.2% [Q1FY27 call]
balance_sheet: Loan-to-deposit ratio is about 86.6% at Mar-26 (₹15.54 vs ₹17.95 lakh cr); borrowings not disclosed in the provided material [AR FY26]
Funding gap is widening: loans +19.6% vs deposits +14.0% and average CASA +12.1% in Q1 FY27; FCNR(B) deposits and debt markets fill the gap [Q1FY27 call]
Capital is being consumed by growth: total CAR fell 17.34% (Dec-25) → 17.18% → 16.84% (Jun-26); CET-1 is 16.19% [Q1FY27 call]
cash_quality: CFO/PAT averaged 2.19x over 3 years, but bank CFO tracks deposit and loan flows, not earnings quality [Numbers]
CFO is volatile: -₹3,771 cr (FY23), ₹1,57,284 cr (FY24), ₹1,22,805 cr (FY25), ₹67,325 cr (FY26); FY26 is only 1.16x PAT [Numbers]
Better earnings-quality test: net NPA 0.33-0.37% and coverage 75.4% (Dec-25) suggest low accrual risk. Recoveries flatter provisions [Q4FY26 call]
narrative_vs_numbers: Agree: 'momentum continues' matches Sep-26 revenue +16.2% and PAT +21.4% YoY after the 2.5%/9.2% trough in Mar-26 [Numbers]
Diverge: the annual report claims 'stable funding', yet deposits lag loans by 5.6pp, and management concedes FCNR leverage will hit NIM [AR FY26]
Profit quality caveat: Q4 provisions fell 90% YoY on written-off recoveries; normalised credit cost of ~50bp implies a higher provision run-rate ahead [Q4FY26 call]
Small gap: management cites consolidated Q1 PAT +13.9%, while Numbers show +12.6% for Jun-26 [Q1FY27 call]
guidance: NIM range-bound in FY27 and 'unlikely to move up' from 4.32%, assuming no policy rate moves [Q4FY26 call]
Opex growth to stay below revenue growth in FY27; cost growth to moderate from 13.2% despite Labour Code costs [Q4FY26 call]
Normalised credit cost about 50bp, adjusting for lumpy recoveries [Q1FY27 call]
FCNR(B) mobilisation over 8-10 weeks to fund growth; international balance sheet to expand 'materially', with some NIM impact [Q1FY27 call]
₹20-25k cr agri PSL book remediation over 'next few months'; provision reversal timing uncertain and pending RBI [Q1FY27 call]

ledger.promised: Loan growth momentum sustains into Q4 [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Loans +15.8% YoY vs 11.5% domestic in Q3; revenue +2.5% QoQ

ledger.promised: LDR not to rise further; may moderate [Q3FY26 call]
Credit card book to grow from Q4 onward [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Analysts flagged the card book contracting for a second quarter at Q4 call

ledger.promised: Unsecured/retail growth to pick up from muted levels [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Retail growth 7.2% → 9.5% → 12.0%; card and PL figures not disclosed

ledger.promised: Opex growth below revenue growth [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Opex not disclosed in Numbers; Sep-26 revenue +16.2% YoY

ledger.promised: No capital raise needed; 17.34% CAR adequate [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: No raise disclosed; CAR down to 16.84% by Jun-26

ledger.promised: Agri PSL remediation and provision reversal in next few months [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: Sep-26 quarter reported; reversal not identifiable in Numbers

bull: Earnings are re-accelerating: PAT YoY went -2.6% → 21.4% in three quarters, and H1 FY27 PAT is up 17.0% [Numbers]
Asset quality is clean: net NPA 0.35%, 75.4% coverage, and 71.9% of corporate loans rated A- or better [AR FY26]
Valuation of 15.9x TTM P/E and 2.6x book for 15.9% ROE and 17-23% PAT CAGR [Numbers]
bear: Growth is funded by wholesale and FCNR money: deposits trail loans by 5.6pp, with an admitted NIM drag [Q1FY27 call]
Profit is flattered by recoveries; reverting to ~50bp credit cost could absorb part of PBT growth [Q4FY26 call]
Capital is eroding: CAR fell 50bp in two quarters while loans grew 19.6%, and business banking grew 28.2% amid an energy shock and El Niño [Q1FY27 call]
questions: What LDR ceiling will you tolerate if deposits keep lagging loans by 5pp?
How many bp of NIM will FCNR leverage cost in FY27?
How much of Q2 FY27 PAT came from recoveries or provision write-backs?
Has RBI approved the agri PSL remediation, and what reversal amount is expected?

annual_report.business: ICICI Bank Limited is India's leading financial services provider offering retail, corporate and business banking. Serves customers through loans, deposits, payments, investments and wealth management products. Generates revenue through net interest margins, service fees, commissions and treasury operations.

segments.name: Retail Banking
segments.comment: Consumer loans, deposits, credit cards, insurance products

segments.name: Corporate Banking
segments.comment: Corporate lending, transaction banking, treasury services

segments.name: Business Banking
segments.comment: SME lending and comprehensive banking solutions

segments.name: Private Banking & Wealth Management
segments.comment: High-net-worth individuals' banking and investment needs

annual_report.revenue_mix: India-focused with overseas coverage for India-linked business. Loan portfolio ₹15,538.93 billion; deposits ₹17,946.25 billion at March 31, 2026. Diverse customer segments across geographies and sectors.
strategy: Customer-360° approach serving complete banking needs across ecosystems and value chains
Micromarket-focused expansion with localized strategies and 7,511 business centres network
Generative AI and digital transformation for efficiency, customer service and innovation
Process simplification and decongestion to enhance customer experience and turnaround times
Strategic partnerships with fintechs, platforms and ecosystem players for growth
annual_report.outlook: Profitable growth with 7.1% PBT growth in FY2026. Focus on capital preservation, asset quality (NPA at 0.33%), stable funding, and market share expansion through enhanced distribution and operational capabilities.
annual_report.capex_plans: Investing in technology platforms, cybersecurity, expanded data centres, AI/ML capabilities and digital channels. Added 528 business centres in FY2026.
risks: Credit risk managed through granular portfolio with 71.9% corporate loans internally rated A- and above
Operational and cyber risks requiring strengthened cybersecurity and data privacy measures
Liquidity risk managed through stable funding profile and growing deposit franchise
Regulatory and compliance risk in evolving banking and technology landscape
annual_report.flags: Related party transactions with ICICI Prudential Life Insurance and ICICI Lombard (subsidiaries) and India Infradebt Limited (associate) for FY2028 being approved at 32nd AGM. Multiple executive compensation revisions and director re-appointments.
